fit: curcumin and cognition after sleep deprivation
assessment: Rats received isolated curcumin in a sleep-deprivation model. Radial-maze learning and memory outcomes give no fall count or culinary ground turmeric comparison.
Hen egg-white lysozyme was a laboratory protein model. Fall refers to a structural region rather than a patient event. No egg ingestion or change in fall frequency.

fit: whole eggs in a high-protein diet and MRI muscle composition
assessment: In 22 older adults a higher-protein diet that included whole eggs gave largely inconclusive MRI results. DXA lean mass and measures of muscle composition are separate from falls. Egg preparation and protein were not independently assigned.

fit: egg-based recipes and baseline-adjusted physical performance
assessment: Of 100 participants assigned recipes and spice packets or control, Short Physical Performance Battery groups were imbalanced at baseline (7.81 vs 9.32). Adjustment did not identify a clear treatment effect on performance. No comparably measured fall frequency or individual poaching effect.

fit: dried egg-white protein and physical function in older women
assessment: The public original reports inconclusive between-group strength and function measures. The full report and underlying fall item results remain unavailable. The trial used dried egg white, not poached eggs.
